## T2: Mechanical accelerator

A massless thread makes $N$ turns around statically fixed cylinder, as shown in the figure. Initially, the free (unwound) ends of the thread are parallel to the axis $X$. Then, a heavy point-like object $P$ is attached to one end of the thread while the other end is pulled with a constant velocity $u$ along $X$. Find the maximum velocity attained by the heavy object.

<image_1>

The thread is inextendable and flexible. Suppose that the turns of the thread are wound tightly to one another and are placed practically in the same plane, perpendicular to the cylinder axis. Neglect any friction in the system. Do not consider the force of gravity.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a fixed cylinder, a thin blue string is tightly wound many turns around the cylinder, the left free end is connected to weight P, the right free end is pulled along the horizontal X direction, and an arrow marks velocity u; the bracket N in the figure indicates the number of turns of winding, and both free ends are parallel to the X direction. Reasoning: Let the radius of the cylinder be R, and let θ denote the angle already unwound from the cylinder, with θ increasing from 0 to 2πN. Since the thin string is inextensible, the right end pulls out string length at velocity u, so the rate of change of the arc length unwound from the cylinder satisfies R dθ/dt = u. Weight P is the endpoint of a segment of tangent thin string unwound from a fixed circle, so its trajectory is the involute of a circle. Take the contact point C(θ)=R(cosθ, sinθ), and the tangential unit vector τ(θ)=(sinθ, -cosθ), then the endpoint can be written as r_P(θ)=C(θ)+R(1+θ)τ(θ). Differentiating with respect to θ gives |dr_P/dθ|=R(1+θ), so the instantaneous velocity of P is v_P=R(1+θ)dθ/dt=u(1+θ). This velocity increases as θ increases, and the maximum value is obtained when all N turns have been unwound, namely θ=2πN. Therefore v_max=u(2πN+1).

raw_record.question_text:
Mechanical accelerator

A massless thread makes $N$ turns around a statically fixed cylinder, as shown in the figure. Initially, the free (unwound) ends of the thread are parallel to the axis $X$. Then, a heavy point-like object $P$ is attached to one end of the thread while the other end is pulled with a constant velocity $u$ along $X$. Find the maximum velocity attained by the heavy object.

The thread is inextendable and flexible. Suppose that the turns of the thread are wound tightly to one another and are placed practically in the same plane, perpendicular to the cylinder axis. Neglect any friction in the system. Do not consider the force of gravity.

method.method_draft: Use an explicit involute-of-a-circle parametrization. First read the figure as a fixed cylinder with many tight turns of thread, the heavy point P attached to the left free end, and the other free end pulled horizontally to the right along the X direction with speed u; the bracket N labels the number of turns. From the text, use that the thread is inextensible/flexible, the cylinder is fixed, the turns lie essentially in one transverse plane, and friction/gravity are neglected. Let R be the cylinder radius and let θ be the angular amount of thread that has been unwound from the cylinder, increasing from 0 to 2πN. Since the pulled end removes arc length at speed u, R dθ/dt = u. The point P is the end of a tangent string unwinding from a fixed circle, so its trajectory is an involute; differentiating the involute geometry gives an instantaneous speed factor v_P = R(1+θ) dθ/dt. Therefore v_P = u(1+θ), which is largest when the full N turns have unwound, θ=2πN, giving v_max = u(2πN+1).
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中有一个固定圆柱，蓝色细线在圆柱上紧密绕了多圈，左侧自由端连接重物 P，右侧自由端沿水平 X 方向被拉动，箭头标出速度 u；图中括号 N 标示绕线圈数，两个自由端都与 X 方向平行。

推理：设圆柱半径为 R，令 θ 表示已经从圆柱上解开的角度，θ 从 0 增加到 2πN。由于细线不可伸长，右端以速度 u 拉出线长，所以圆柱上被解开的弧长变化率满足 R dθ/dt = u。重物 P 是一段切线细线从固定圆上展开的端点，因此其轨迹是圆的渐开线。取接触点 C(θ)=R(cosθ, sinθ)，切向单位矢量 τ(θ)=(sinθ, -cosθ)，则端点可写成 r_P(θ)=C(θ)+R(1+θ)τ(θ)。对 θ 求导得 |dr_P/dθ|=R(1+θ)，所以 P 的瞬时速度为 v_P=R(1+θ)dθ/dt=u(1+θ)。该速度随 θ 增大而增大，最大值在全部 N 圈解开时取得，即 θ=2πN。因此 v_max=u(2πN+1)。

method.method_draft: Use a differential constraint/Jacobian argument without writing the full trajectory. From the image, identify the same horizontal pulling end with speed u, the object P at the opposite free end, and N full wraps around the fixed cylinder. From the text, impose inextensibility and ideal frictionless contact, so only geometry determines the velocity ratio. Let q be the displacement of the pulled end; qdot = u. Let θ=q/R be the angular amount of thread peeled from the cylinder, so θ ranges from 0 to 2πN. For a small pull dq, the endpoint P is displaced by two contributions: the direct advance of the thread, dq, plus the motion caused by rotation of the tangent line through dθ=dq/R while the already-unwound tangent length is Rθ, giving an extra displacement Rθ dθ = θ dq. Thus dx_P = (1+θ)dq, so v_P = dx_P/dt = (1+θ)u. The maximum occurs at the largest possible θ, after N turns have been unwound, θ=2πN, hence v_max=u(2πN+1).
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中有一个固定圆柱，细线在圆柱侧面紧密缠绕了多圈，左侧自由端连接重物 P，右侧自由端沿水平 X 方向被拉出，速度标为 u。图中还用括号标出缠绕圈数为 N，两个自由端最初都近似沿 X 方向。

推理：设圆柱半径为 R，右端被拉出的位移为 q，则 qdot = u。由于细线不可伸长，右端拉出长度 dq 会使缠绕在圆柱上的线退绕一小段，对应退绕角 dθ = dq/R。因此令 θ = q/R，θ 从 0 增加到全部 N 圈退绕完时的 2πN。

对重物 P 的位移作微分约束分析。右端多拉出 dq 时，P 端首先有一份直接由线长传递造成的位移 dq。此外，由于切线方向随着退绕角改变 dθ，而已经退绕出的切线段长度为 Rθ，这会额外带动 P 端位移 Rθ dθ。代入 dθ = dq/R，额外位移为 Rθ(dq/R)=θdq。

所以 P 的微小位移为 dx_P = dq + θdq = (1+θ)dq。两边对时间求导，得到 v_P = dx_P/dt = (1+θ)u。随着 θ 增大，v_P 单调增大，因此最大速度出现在全部 N 圈刚退绕完时，即 θ = 2πN。

因此最大速度为 v_max = u(1+2πN)。

Mechanical accelerator

A massless thread makes $N$ turns around a statically fixed cylinder, as shown in the figure. Initially, the free (unwound) ends of the thread are parallel to the axis $X$. Then, a heavy point-like object $P$ is attached to one end of the thread while the other end is pulled with a constant velocity $u$ along $X$. Find the maximum velocity attained by the heavy object.

The thread is inextendable and flexible. Suppose that the turns of the thread are wound tightly to one another and are placed practically in the same plane, perpendicular to the cylinder axis. Neglect any friction in the system. Do not consider the force of gravity.

Image description: In the figure there is a fixed cylinder, a thin blue string is tightly wound many turns around the cylinder, the left free end is connected to weight P, the right free end is pulled along the horizontal X direction, and an arrow marks velocity u; the bracket N in the figure indicates the number of turns of winding, and both free ends are parallel to the X direction.

Reasoning: Let the radius of the cylinder be R, and let θ denote the angle already unwound from the cylinder, with θ increasing from 0 to 2πN. Since the thin string is inextensible, the right end pulls out string length at velocity u, so the rate of change of the arc length unwound from the cylinder satisfies R dθ/dt = u. Weight P is the endpoint of a segment of tangent thin string unwound from a fixed circle, so its trajectory is the involute of a circle. Take the contact point C(θ)=R(cosθ, sinθ), and the tangential unit vector τ(θ)=(sinθ, -cosθ), then the endpoint can be written as r_P(θ)=C(θ)+R(1+θ)τ(θ). Differentiating with respect to θ gives |dr_P/dθ|=R(1+θ), so the instantaneous velocity of P is v_P=R(1+θ)dθ/dt=u(1+θ). This velocity increases as θ increases, and the maximum value is obtained when all N turns have been unwound, namely θ=2πN. Therefore v_max=u(2πN+1).
